messages:
Alice: FYI saw a big p99 spike during the 11:22 burst test. Looks correlated with autoscaler scale-up lag + kernel switch.
Ben: Can you paste the flame/profiler output? Is KV cold misses up too?
Alice: attaching small excerpt from trace:
```
PROF: sample 2023-11-15T11:22:05
kernel: aten_fused_attention_v2 chosen at t=0.21s
batch_size distribution: 1,1,2,8,8,8,16,16,16
kv_cache_hits: 62% -> drops to 18% for first 30s after scaleup
p50/p95/p99: 45ms / 210ms / 920ms
```
Carla: Oof. That batch distribution shows a long tail of small microbatches during the warm window. Thermostat/prober probably ramped incorrectly and picked a kernel that favors larger batches.
Dan: Which kernel fallback was used? If it picks a kernel optimized for big microbatches, single-request latencies blow up.
Alice: Right — the kernel selector picked "fast-path-vec" after prober samples biased by queued backlog. It matches high throughput but has worse single-request ramp-up.
Emma: Two levers: reduce microbatch target during detected surge, or force kv_preheat on scaleup. Both reduce p99 but affect throughput. Any numbers on throughput loss?
Ben: Quick sim: reducing microbatch target from 8->4 lowers throughput ~12% in steady-state but cuts p99 tail by ~40% during warm periods in our replay.
Carla: Also worth noting KV preheat adds ~0.7s to instance startup cost but increases early KV hit ratio from 18%->70% for the first 30s. That reduces cold-tail badly.
Alice: Proposal: thermostat change + conservative kernel probe for first 15s after scaleup: probe sample_size=20, prefer small-batch kernel if p95>200ms. Rolling experiment next deploy?
Dan: Sounds reasonable. Add metric guardrails: p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_ratio, batch_size_histogram, kernel_variant, and downstream error rate.
Emma: I'll add an experiment tag and run against production-canary traffic for 2h with circuit breaker to revert if p99 > 1.2s.
infra-bot: Scheduled experiment: exp/thermostat-scaleup-20231115, start=1743508000, duration=7200s. Will collect: perf-traces, kv-stats, batch-hist.
Ben: One more: log the time between scale decision and first allocation ready (scaleup_lag). If that > 3s, we should consider burst reserve.
Carla: Agreed. For the experiment config:
```
thermostat:
  post_scale_probe_window_s: 15
  probe_sample_size: 20
  prefer_small_kernel_on_warm: true
microbatch:
  target: 4
  max_latency_slo_ms: 300
kv:
  preheat_on_scaleup: true
```
Alice: I'll own the rollout and collect traces. If we see >30% throughput regression in steady-state we'll rollback. Otherwise we keep and iterate on kernel heuristics.
Emma: Thanks — schedule looks good. Will ping once the canary starts. :thumbsup:
